topic: past-only adaptive priority proposals remain unbiased while proposal quality is learned online

public_evidence.source: Ryu and Boyd, Adaptive Importance Sampling via Stochastic Convex Programming
public_evidence.result: For exponential-family proposals, importance-sampling variance is convex in the natural parameter. Their adaptive sampler updates the proposal while accumulating the estimate; the estimator is unbiased and its variance is asymptotically optimal over the proposal family under the paper's assumptions.

public_evidence.source: Lu, Rainforth, Zhou, van de Meent, Teh, On Exploration, Exploitation and Learning in Adaptive Importance Sampling / Daisee
public_evidence.result: Treats adaptive importance sampling as an online-learning problem and gives a sublinear cumulative pseudo-regret guarantee, reinforcing that exploration/exploitation of proposal choices is itself an optimization problem rather than a fixed heuristic.

public_evidence.source: Finke, Johansen, Lee, Murray, Resampling in conditional SMC algorithms
public_evidence.result: Properly weighted adaptive resampling is compatible with unbiased SMC normalizing-constant estimation. This remains the particle-resampling correctness layer beneath the past-only adaptive priority policy.

derived_martingale_argument.setup: At step t choose q_t from history F_{t-1}; require q_t(i)>0 whenever W_i>0. Draw A_t~q_t and Y_t with E[Y_t|A_t=i,F_{t-1}]=p_i under the base continuation law.
derived_martingale_argument.conditional_expectation: E[X_t|F_{t-1}] = sum_i q_t(i) W_i p_i/q_t(i) = theta = sum_i W_i p_i
derived_martingale_argument.consequence: q_t may depend arbitrarily on past samples, past proxy-quality estimates, or a past-only choice of epsilon_t without biasing the running risk average, provided the exact q_t used for each draw is logged and support/base-transition conditions hold.
derived_martingale_argument.scope: This proves expectation preservation for the one-step branch-risk abstraction. Sequential environment/tool proposal changes still require the separate trajectory likelihood ratios identified in r108-r109.

past_only_second_moment_monitor.unbiased_observation_from_current_q_t: H_t(q') = W_{A_t}^2 Y_t / (q_t(A_t) q'_i) evaluated at i=A_t, so E[H_t(q')|F_{t-1}] = S(q')
past_only_second_moment_monitor.defensive_bound: If both current and candidate proposals have floors q_t(i)>=epsilon_min W_i and q'(i)>=epsilon_min W_i, then 0<=H_t(q')<=1/epsilon_min^2 for Bernoulli Y_t.
past_only_second_moment_monitor.use: Past draws can therefore compare the second moments of future epsilon/proposal candidates without using future outcomes. A confidence-sequence or conservative bounded-mean gate can choose the next epsilon from past data while the risk estimator itself remains conditionally unbiased regardless of whether that choice is variance-optimal.

toy_pilot_then_adapt_stress.purpose: Check that a past-only data-dependent epsilon choice avoids the clear fixed-epsilon harm from r109 without introducing detectable bias in a synthetic rare-event model.
toy_pilot_then_adapt_stress.selection_rule: choose epsilon minimizing the pilot unbiased second-moment estimate over the fixed candidate grid; use selected q only for later evaluation draws
toy_pilot_then_adapt_stress.interpretation: The past-only adaptive rule showed no detectable bias and modestly beat all-base sampling while avoiding the harmful fixed epsilon=0.2 configuration. This is a finite synthetic engineering check, not a theorem or agent benchmark.

negative_or_scope_evidence: Past-only adaptivity preserves expectation but does not guarantee good variance; an unstable or noisy selection rule may still waste samples.
The simple empirical second-moment selector can overfit rare pilot failures. A sequential confidence/regularization layer is still needed before treating epsilon adaptation as robust.
Ryu-Boyd's asymptotic optimality is for their exponential-family stochastic-convex-programming setting; it does not directly prove optimality of the discrete branch-priority mixture used here.
Daisee's regret theorem supports online proposal learning but is not an SMC normalizing-constant theorem for stochastic agent trees.
next_tests: Replace pilot argmin with an anytime bounded-second-moment confidence gate that only moves epsilon away from 1 when a candidate is certified to reduce S(q) by a meaningful margin.
Test predictable epsilon adaptation under proxy drift/nonstationarity and compare against fixed base, fixed priority and oracle epsilon using common random paths.
Extend from iid descendant selection to dependent/systematic sibling resampling while preserving Finke proper weighting.
Investigate agent/tool settings where base transition likelihoods are unavailable and determine whether replay must remain under the base environment law for identifiable deployment-risk estimation.
